chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The oath is returned to the claimant.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the oath if the claimant has no proof?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'rad al-yamin' (returning the oath), establishing that in the absence of formal testimony or proof, the burden of verification shifts to the claimant. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a critical procedural safeguard, ensuring that those who assert a right without evidence must substantiate their claim through a solemn oath, thereby preventing frivolous litigation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The swearing would be turned upon the claimant’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the oath can be turned to the plaintiff.”
